title: Optimal Learning from Label Proportions with General Loss Functions
claim: Our debiased estimator achieves lower test loss than baselines across most dataset and aggregation-size settings, with the gap widening as bags grow.
layout: 5 line-plot panels, 2 over 3 grid, shared legend, shaded error bands
description: Five small line plots in a two-over-three grid, one per dataset: Adult, Higgs, MNIST Even vs Odd, CIFAR-10 Animal vs Machine, and CIFAR-10 Cat vs Rest. Each plot has bag size on the x-axis (powers of two, 2^4 to 2^10) and log loss on the y-axis. Each shows three lines with markers and translucent standard-error bands: EasyLLP in blue, GeneralUPM in orange, and PM in green. A legend sits in the upper left of every panel. Loss rises with bag size and shoots up sharply at 2^10, running off the top of several plots. GeneralUPM (orange) is mostly lowest or near-lowest at large bag sizes. PM (green) is best at small bag sizes and on MNIST. The eye goes to the diverging curves and the steep rise on the right.
caption: Minimum average test log loss achieved for each k, optimized across various learning rates and stopping epochs. Results are averaged over 10 repetitions, with error bars representing one standard error.
abstract: Motivated by problems in online advertising, we address the task of Learning from Label Proportions (LLP). We introduce a novel and versatile low-variance debiasing methodology to learn from aggregate label information, significantly advancing the state of the art in LLP. Our debiasing approach exhibits remarkable flexibility, seamlessly accommodating a broad spectrum of practically relevant loss functions across both binary and multi-class classification settings. By carefully combining our estimators with standard techniques, we improve sample complexity guarantees for a large class of losses of practical relevance. We also empirically validate the efficacy of our proposed approach across a diverse array of benchmark datasets, demonstrating compelling empirical advantages over standard baselines.
